newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Wool prices gain sharply at New Zealand sales.
newsitem.headline: Wool prices gain sharply at New Zealand sales.

text.p: New Zealand wool prices gained sharply at Napier and Christchurch sales on Thursday, the market indicator firming 15 cents to 441 NZ cents per kg clean.
Wools of NZ said the fine indicator gained 15 cents to 822, medium by 16 to 524, strong by 12 to 391 and lambs by 33 to 402.

The 4,195-clean-tonne offer mostly comprised 48 percent crossbred fleece, 14 percent second shear, 14 percent lambswool, 5.0 percent cotts, 5.0 percent halfbred fleece, 4.0 percent bulky skirtings, 4.0 percent second shear bellies and pieces and 1.0 percent merino fleece.
Sixteen percent of the offer was passed in.
Prices were two percent up for merino fleece.
Halfbred fleece, 24 micron, was unchanged. 25-28 micron was up 2.0-3.0 percent and 29 micron and stronger was up by 2.0 percent.
Crossbred fleece 32-34 micron, was generally unchanged while 35 micron and stronger rose by 2.5 to 5.0 percent.

First Lambs wool, 27-30 micron, was 7.5 to 10 percent up, 31 micron was up by 4.0 percent and second lambs wool was up by 10-12. Bulky skirtings rose by 3.0 percent and second shear bellies and pieces gained by 2.5 to 7.5 percent.
